title: Prompt archive publication journal v1
description: A closed, payload-free, hash-chained publication journal. Every generation records the immutable plan and all intended artifact refs. The response pointer is immutable create-or-verify. Every authoritative or legacy latest-response write binds a predecessor-independent ordered content intent and uses one physical cross-process lock collocated with and derived from the external latest-response target, never an archive/runtime root. Under that lock recovery compares intent order, dynamically derives a wrapper from the current predecessor only when needed, treats a later ordered slot as a safe superseded result, and reconciles mixed content/sidecar state before compatibility_published. Success advances intent -> blobs -> manifest -> pointer -> archive locator -> compatibility outputs -> complete. Abort is valid only before pointer publication. Prior immutable generation bytes are retained and bound by generation plus SHA-256.

previous_journal_sha256.description: SHA-256 of the exact canonical UTF-8 bytes in the retained immutable previous generation file; null only for generation zero.

pendingRegistryJournal.description: The exact key-level bounded-registry precondition and mutation intent for this immutable journal generation. shard project/id and precondition entry operation/recovery/plan refs must semantically equal the enclosing journal. Under the shard lock the writer loads the latest valid shard, compares only this recovery_key to precondition_entry or the exact intended result, preserves unrelated entries, deterministically rebases the key mutation, and publishes the next whole-shard CAS generation; unrelated changes retry, while only a differing same-key entry conflicts. Nonterminal generations bind their own canonical journal ref after journal CAS; terminal generations remove the exact entry. Binding tokens avoid impossible journal/registry content-hash cycles. Startup enumerates only 256 stable shard keys. A planned entry recovers index-before-journal; a journaled entry recovers the bound journal; terminal journal persistence precedes idempotent removal.

latestOrdering.description: A deterministic total order compared lexicographically by source_revision, occurrence_id, then operation_id, but only after revision_authority exactly matches. The source revision is allocated from a durable project/slot high-water mark that is never reset by a process, launcher, or runtime-root restart. If that continuity cannot be restored, publication fails closed instead of allocating a lower revision.

revisionAuthority.description: The stable V1 revision domain is the enclosing (project_id, slot_scope, slot_id). Epoch rollover is not defined in V1: the durable high-water mark must be restored, or allocation and publication fail closed.

latestBootstrapPrecondition.description: Used only while no sidecar is enrolled. Under the one physical lock collocated with the resolved external latest-response target, the writer observes the target, durably publishes the intended bytes plus retained/current enrollment intent, and only then may unlock. That discoverable marker makes every legacy writer drain or fail closed. The writer performs the non-nested pending-registry mutation while no latest/operation/response lock is held, then reacquires the same latest lock, revalidates marker and observation, and holds it through content and first-slot reconciliation. Every code path capable of writing legacy latest-response bytes, including default legacy with no archive root and the legacy writer accompanying shadow mode, locates and takes that same lock. Once any valid marker/slot exists, ordered intent semantics supersede the bootstrap observation.

latestContentIntent.description: The exact predecessor-independent content intent copied from the immutable publication plan. No mutable whole-slot generation or predecessor ref is frozen here. Under the stable project-global lock a same intent succeeds, a greater current order yields superseded, and a lower order derives generation=current+1 and previous_slot_id=current before reconciling content and sidecar.

legacyLatestJournalState.description: The compact state machine shared by every normal legacy latest-response publication and operator rollback. Every event occurred_at must semantically equal the corresponding retry-stable frozen timestamp: intent_at, legacy_payload_verified_at, compatibility_published_at, completed_at, or aborted_at.
